title: English — Grade 2 Entrance
subject: english

questions.prompt:
Choose the correct missing word:

My friend .... three best friends. They play together every day.

Add the correct punctuation mark to the following sentence:

Can I draw a rainbow

Find all the capital letters in the following sentence: [Type the capital letters you find, separated by commas.]

My sister has two dogs, Jack and Bubu.

questions.criteria:
The student writes their own name.
1 point: the name begins with a capital letter.
1 point: the rest of the name is written in lowercase letters (no random capitals).
1 point: the name is written completely and legibly (no missing letters).

questions.prompt:
Look and read. Put a tick (√) if the sentence matches the picture or a cross (×) if it does not.

**These are books.**

Look and read. Put a tick (√) if the sentence matches the picture or a cross (×) if it does not.

**This is a window.**

Look and read. Put a tick (√) if the sentence matches the picture or a cross (×) if it does not.

**This is a water bottle.**

Look at the picture and read. Write **yes** or **no**.

Examples: "The mom and the child are looking through the window." — no. "You can see an armchair in the room." — yes.

**The dad is in the room.**

Look at the picture and read. Write **yes** or **no**.

**There is a green armchair in the room.**

Look at the picture and read. Write **yes** or **no**.

**The child is sitting.**

Look at the picture and read. Write **yes** or **no**.

**You can see books in the room.**

Read the sentence and use the picture to decide whether it is **True** or **False**.

**The cat has a hat.**

Read the sentence and use the picture to decide whether it is **True** or **False**.

**A rat is in the pan.**

Read the sentence and use the picture to decide whether it is **True** or **False**.

**The man has a net.**

Read the sentence and use the picture to decide whether it is **True** or **False**.

**The man has a bag on his back.**

Read the sentence and use the picture to decide whether it is **True** or **False**.

**The can is in the pan.**

questions.criteria:
1 point: the student writes at least one complete, relevant sentence about their mom.
1 point: ideas are understandable and on topic (e.g. what she looks like, what she does, why the student loves her).
1 point: basic grammar, capitalization, and spelling appropriate for Grade 2 (sentence starts with a capital letter, ends with a full stop).

importNotes: Source footer says 'Total: /20 points' but the printed per-question marks sum to 23 (1+1+3+3+3+4+5+3); teacher must decide which is authoritative.
Q4 'Write your name' (3 pts) grades handwriting features (capital first letter, lowercase rest, legibility) that a typed answer cannot fully demonstrate — teacher review advised.
Q3 'circle the capital letters' was adapted to typing the letters (answerKey 'M, J, B'); accept any order/format of the three letters.
Printed per-question marks sum to 23 but the cover footer says 'Total: /20' — a human should confirm which is intended.
Test duration is not stated anywhere in the document; defaulted to 60 minutes (primary).

Q4 'Write your name below' (3 points) was a handwriting task on guide lines in the source; adapted for typed input with criteria on capitalization/completeness — handwriting formation itself cannot be assessed digitally.
Q3 'Circle all capital letters' adapted to typing the capital letters (answer key: M, J, B).
Q5 (3 pts), Q6 (4 pts), Q7 (5 pts) were split into 1-point sub-questions; per-item marks were not printed individually but item counts match the totals.
Q6.3 'The child is sitting' keyed as 'no' — in the photo the child appears to be standing at the table while the mom sits; worth a quick teacher check.

Q7 statements were transcribed from the worksheet image (media/image14.png); the person in the picture has a beard and holds a net, a rat sits in the pan, the bag is on the floor, and the can is on the counter — keys set accordingly (False, True, True, False, False).
